Math 131H discussion section, week 11 (Chapter 3 review). Covers sections 3.1–3.6, 3.10 and 3.11.

Chapter 3 review: all the derivative rules in one place

Worked solutions to the Chapter 3 review worksheet. It covers the power, product, quotient and chain rules, then inverse trig and log derivatives, implicit and logarithmic differentiation, derivatives from a table, linear approximation, and hyperbolic functions. Parts tagged optional are extra practice. On the worksheet they are collected on the last page, including Examples 8 and 9.

1. Basic rules 2. Logs and inverse trig 3. Implicit 4. Log differentiation 5. Table 6. Linear approximation 7. Hyperbolic 8. Horizontal tangents 9. Trig limits
Before you start

Which rule when?

Most mistakes on a Chapter 3 exam come from picking the wrong rule, not from the algebra. Before you differentiate, ask what the last operation in the function is. That operation decides the rule.

The function looks likeUseExamples on this sheet
a sum of powers, roots, rewrite as , then the power rule1(a)
product rule1(d), 1(g), 2(b), 7(a)
quotient rule, or simplify first1(b), 1(f), 7(c)
a function of a functionchain rule, one factor per layer1(c), 1(e), 2(a), 2(c), 7(b)
and mixed in an equationimplicit differentiation3
in both base and exponent, or a big product/quotientlogarithmic differentiation4
only numbers giventhe same rules, reading values off the table5
